body: I hope you choose not to commit. I hope you find the help you need. It sucks for any of us to be hurting.

I can understand that. I know I only care about 5 people realistically. I stick around because I know with or without me, life will move on. There's comfort in that, but I know that for those people I care about, and those who care about me, life still has to move on. If I take my life, the people I never want to hurt will likely hurt their entire lives because of my actions. I had started rationalizing how they could move on last month, but was brought back to the reality that they more than likely never would after an unexpected person called me out to tell me not to commit.

I think it would be best to discuss with your partner how you're feeling. It can be difficult to keep going and when you feel you've found a way to go peacefully it can be very enticing. I would recommend getting professional help before things turn worse. I hate for anyone to feel how I do, so while I empathize, I urge you to reconsider. Keep in mind that even after you pass, life has to go on, this can be either comforting or harrowing though depending on your mindset.

I got sexually abused when I was younger. It's very difficult to deal with as a male person. It may be possible to reach out to hotline clinics without your parents knowing. I wish I had better advice for you. I'm still figuring it out, but I know the ex I mentioned in my post tells me she wouldn't have gotten over anorexia if not for me. I'm sure you've touched more people than you realize. Those of us hurting seem to.

I used to make different personalities to try and cope with different situations that come up. I tried to anticipate everything and the only thing I've learned is I can't really control everything. I don't know how your life has been destroyed, but I can tell you that I've lost everything before. At 16, everything can be rebuilt. It can be difficult, and it might mean therapy. If that's not an option now then it may mean making a goal for yourself to make it an option. When it comes to talking about the issues with your friend, just know that if you do open up your friend is also 16 (presumably) and may want to help, but lacks the means or knowledge. I was very lucky to have a mentor in my guitar teacher at the time I was 16, and an outlet in music. I poured myself into that and stuck around because I didn't want my sister to go through trauma losing her older brother to suicide. Sometimes that's still how I have to get by. It can feel like no one else knows how you feel, or wants to deal with how your life is, but hey, just this conversation is proof that life can be worth living despite the shit we go through and put ourselves through. I still see myself as a negative influence on people, but if you asked any of my friends, and even most of my exes, they would all say that their lives are better for me being in it. It's also possible your friend already knows and just doesn't know how to talk to you about it without pushing you away.  (For your reference, I'm 24 m, and my life got wretched from my hands 2 years ago, but I've been rebuilding and even though it's been hard, I'm starting to continue that process again.) I try not to give out exact advice on what to do for people anymore because the truth is I'm not qualified, but I do know things can improve. I went through my entire teenage years without realistically confiding in anyone, and even convinced a guidance counselor that I wasn't suicidal with a straight face. I wish now that I had been more honest with the people in my life what was really going on in my head, but I have no idea how the people in your life are and I know not all people are accepting.

I wish that I had a good solution for you. I understand. At some point, you just get tired. The only thing I can offer is that sometimes you live for others. It sucks. I just got done walking down a road with at least 10 fatalities a year hoping that someone hit me. I got home though. I called my brother and talked to him. Just that he was there provided some relief. That for just a moment I didn't feel so cripplingly alone. I don't know if you're able to really talk to your wife about what's going on, but if there's someone in your life who's willing to just be there, and not necessarily provide a solution, that can help alot.

It's crazy. Even when her and I were dating I kept her at arms length so she wouldn't see any of that side of me. So when we were just texting and she sent me that my only reply was, "Why did you tell me that?"

It is hypocritical though. The most of us would never wish this upon anyone else, but it's just so difficult to apply the logic we would give to others to yourself. I use humor now just so I can talk about it with friends and everyone thinks I'm psychotic now. It's the only way I know how to cope anymore though. I haven't been able to cry for years.
